newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek inflation drop to lead to lower rates-min.
newsitem.headline: Greek inflation drop to lead to lower rates-min.

text.p: Greece's National Economy Minister Yannos Papandoniou told reporters that the fall of inflation to 6.8 percent year-on-year in January would lead to a new round of rate cuts in bank lending and government securities.

"The drop of inflation to 6.8 percent year-on-year for the first time in 25 years is a very positive development," said Papandoniou. "..it is important because it leads to a new reduction in lending rates."
Greek revised CPI inflation dropped to 6.8 percent year-on-year in January from 7.3 percent in December. Inflation stood at 7.5 percent year-on-year in December on the basis of the old CPI index.
He added that interest rates on government securities would be slashed and inflation was falling faster than expected. --Dimitris Kontogiannis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
